output:
### Summary

I reviewed commit 10d228d (`tests/run`, `tests/00-harness.sh`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `docs/spec.md`) against issue 30's four criteria, reading all four files in full plus `tests/lib.sh`, `scripts/gate.sh` and the author's work note. The four files are identical to HEAD in the worktree (0 diff lines). I ran 17 mutants of `tests/run` against the new test block and 12 behaviour probes, all on a `git archive HEAD` copy at `/tmp/claude-1000/-home-alex-blast-off--claude-worktrees-pending-items-53932d/60b15296-819e-491a-8ffe-34b3bd988f86/scratchpad/rev.vBKlN4`. Criterion 1 works and its test is real: reverting `tests/run` to origin/main turns it red, and 12 of 17 mutants are killed. No CRITICAL or HIGH finding. The gaps: 4 non-equivalent mutants survive (two in the re-run path), criterion 2 has no test and has never executed on GitHub, and the one new dependency, `actions/upload-artifact@v4`, declares a Node runtime GitHub removed from runners on 2026-09-23.

### Findings

#### CRITICAL

None.

#### HIGH

None.

#### MEDIUM

- **Title:** The re-run assertion is satisfied by the first run's leftovers; two re-run mutants survive
- **Location:** `tests/00-harness.sh:33-34`
- **Description:** Line 33 runs the gate a second time with `|| true` and never reads its verdict. Line 34 checks only that `kept/01-ok/tmp.*` is absent and `kept/01-ok/out` exists, and run 1 already made both true. Measured, with the new block passing (`BLOCK-PASS`, rc=0) in both cases:
  - `mkdir -p "$KEEP"` changed to `mkdir "$KEEP"` (line 19): every re-run into an existing keep dir aborts before any scenario with `mkdir: cannot create directory 'k4': File exists`, rc=1, no `GATE:` line.
  - A stale kept dir wins (the new work dir is discarded when `$KEEP/$name` exists): the kept output is from an older run.
  
  The check also depends on GNU `mktemp`'s default `tmp.*` name and looks only at `01-ok`. Nothing asserts that the keep dir holds exactly one subdir per scenario.
- **Suggested fix:** Before the second run, plant `: > kept/01-ok/stale`. Assert the second run's verdict line instead of `|| true`. Assert `ls -A kept/01-ok` is exactly `cwd out`. I ran this variant on the copy: HEAD passes, and it kills the `mkdir`-without-`-p` mutant ("second keep run verdict: mkdir: cannot create directory 'kept': File exists"), the stale-wins mutant and the no-stale-`rm` mutant (both "re-run did not replace the kept dir").

- **Title:** Criterion 2 (the CI wiring) has no test and has never run
- **Location:** `.github/workflows/ci.yml:35-37, 43-48`; no reader in `tests/`
- **Description:** A grep for `ci\.yml`, `upload-artifact` and `BLAST_OFF_TEST_KEEP` across the tree finds no test that reads the workflow, so any edit to these lines passes the gate. The branch is not pushed: `gh pr list --head feat/br-1115-issues/phase-1 --state all` and `gh run list --branch ...` both return `[]`. The keep path is written twice as a literal (line 37 and line 48). If the two drift, or the env block is dropped, the upload step finds nothing, and `if-no-files-found` defaults to `warn` ([upload-artifact README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/actions/upload-artifact/main/README.md)). The step runs only on an already-red job, so the feature would be found broken on the day it is needed.
- **Suggested fix:** Add `if-no-files-found: error` to the step. Pin the wiring in `00-harness` the way `.gitignore` and `.claude/settings.json` are pinned there (lines 47-56): the step env sets `BLAST_OFF_TEST_KEEP`, the upload `path:` is the same string, and the step carries `if: failure()`. Before merge, trigger one deliberately red run on the PR and confirm the artifact holds `<scenario>/out` and a `run.log`.

- **Title:** New dependency `actions/upload-artifact@v4`: floating major tag, three majors behind, targets a removed Node runtime
- **Location:** `.github/workflows/ci.yml:45`
- **Description:** This is the only new dependency in the change. `@v4` is a mutable tag (today it points at `ea165f8d65b6e75b540449e92b4886f43607fa02`), not a SHA, the same convention as the existing `actions/checkout@v4`. Its `action.yml` at `v4` declares `using: 'node20'`; `v7`, the major the README's examples use, declares `using: 'node24'`. GitHub removed Node 20 from runners on 2026-09-23 ([changelog](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-09-23-node-20-is-no-longer-available-in-github-actions/)). This repo's latest CI run (43778239611, 2026-11-16, green) carries the annotation "Node.js 20 is deprecated. The following actions target Node.js 20 but are being forced to run on Node.js 24: actions/checkout@v4". `upload-artifact@v4` would be forced the same way. That combination is unverified, not known broken.
- **Suggested fix:** Use a Node 24 major (v6 or later; v7 is current) and confirm it with the red run above. v7 adds direct single-file upload; a directory `path:` still zips ([releases](https://github.com/actions/upload-artifact/releases)). Pinning to a commit SHA is the stricter option; the repo currently pins neither action.

#### LOW

- **Title:** Keep-dir failures end the gate with exit 1 and no `GATE:` line; the "fails before any scenario" claim is untested
- **Location:** `tests/run:9, 18-19, 34`
- **Description:** Measured:
  - Keep dir under a regular file: rc=1, 0 `GATE:` lines, 0 scenarios run.
  - Keep dir read-only: rc=1, 0 `GATE:` lines, 1 of 2 scenarios run, 1 work dir left in `TMPDIR`.
  - Moving `mkdir -p` into the loop (keep dir made only when the first scenario ends) leaves the new block passing, so the comment on line 18 is unproven.
  
  The header (line 9) lists only `GATE: PASS` and `GATE: FAIL` exits. CI sets the var on every run, so a keep-side fault stops a suite mid-way. The exit stays non-zero, so nothing reads as green, and a failing `rm -rf "$work"` aborted the same way before this change.
- **Suggested fix:** One assertion: an uncreatable keep dir exits non-zero and prints no `PASS`/`FAIL` scenario line. Either document the no-verdict exit in the header, or make a failed `mv` a counted failure instead of an abort.

- **Title:** A keep dir under the repo's `tests/`, `bin/` or `lib/` is linted by the gate's own shellcheck and turns a green gate red
- **Location:** `tests/run:34` with `tests/run:42`; header lines 7-8
- **Description:** Measured from the repo-root copy with one passing fixture scenario that writes a shebang-less `ok/01-ok.sh`, as `tests/00-harness.sh:8` does:
  - Var unset: `GATE: PASS passed=1 failed=0 shellcheck=ok` (33 files).
  - `BLAST_OFF_TEST_KEEP=tests/kept`: `SC2148 (error)` in `tests/kept/01-like-harness/cwd/ok/01-ok.sh`, then `GATE: FAIL passed=1 failed=1 shellcheck=fail`.
  - `BLAST_OFF_TEST_KEEP=kept` at the repo root: PASS.
  
  CI's `runner.temp` path is unaffected. The header does not say where the dir may live.
- **Suggested fix:** Say in the header that the dir must sit outside `bin/`, `lib/` and `tests/`, or refuse such a path at line 19.

- **Title:** The "unset" half only looks at `TMPDIR`
- **Location:** `tests/00-harness.sh:36-37`
- **Description:** A mutant that keeps to a default dir when the var is unset (`KEEP="${BLAST_OFF_TEST_KEEP:-$PWD/always-kept}"`) leaves the block passing: the work dirs left `TMPDIR`, so `ls -A tmp` is empty. The test proves "not left in TMPDIR", not "removed".
- **Suggested fix:** Snapshot the scenario cwd's entries (`ls -A`) before the unset run and assert no new entry apart from `keepfix.out`.

- **Title:** No test distinguishes the absolute-path step
- **Location:** `tests/run:19` (`KEEP="$(cd "$KEEP" && pwd)"`)
- **Description:** Dropping the `cd && pwd` leaves the block passing. The parent shell never changes directory, so a relative keep dir behaves the same for a usable dir (probe: `BLAST_OFF_TEST_KEEP=rel/k` from another cwd lands in that cwd's `rel/k`). Its remaining effect is failing fast on a keep dir that exists but cannot be entered, and that is not tested either.
- **Suggested fix:** Delete the conversion, or keep it and cover it with the uncreatable-dir assertion above.

- **Title:** Job-level timeout or cancel uploads nothing, and an in-flight scenario's dir is not yet in the keep dir
- **Location:** `.github/workflows/ci.yml:14, 44`; `tests/run:34`
- **Description:** A work dir reaches the keep dir only after its scenario ends. A scenario that hits `BLAST_OFF_TEST_TIMEOUT` is covered: it counts as FAIL and its dir is kept (probe: 1 s timeout, `out` holds `before`). The uncovered case is the job reaching `timeout-minutes: 30` or being cancelled. 18 scenarios at the 300 s default allow 90 minutes. The [expressions docs](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/expressions) define `failure()` as "Returns `true` when any previous step of a job fails" and do not say it runs on timeout or cancel. Criterion 2 asks for `if: failure()` exactly, so this is a limit of the spec as written.
- **Suggested fix:** Decide whether `if: failure() || cancelled()` is wanted. If not, record the limit in the ci.yml comment.

- **Title:** A unit-started runner's stderr goes to the journal, which is not in the artifact
- **Location:** `lib/chain.sh:21` ("its error is on stderr (the journal under the unit)"); `tests/11-unit-smoke.sh:27`; `tests/31-resume-after-reset.sh`
- **Description:** `run.log` lives in the job dir under the scenario cwd (`bin/blast-off:60`, `tests/lib.sh:23`), so it is kept. For scenarios that launch through `start`, an aborting runner's own error is in the user journal only.
- **Suggested fix:** If wanted, add a `journalctl --user --no-pager` dump into the keep dir in the failure path. Out of issue 30's wording.

- **Title:** Stale subdirs of scenarios no longer run stay in the keep dir
- **Location:** `tests/run:34`
- **Description:** Probe: a pre-existing `k2/99-gone` survives a run that keeps `01-ok` and `02-ok`. A local reused keep dir can mix runs. CI's fresh `runner.temp` is unaffected.
- **Suggested fix:** Note it in the header, or leave it.

- **Title:** ci.yml comment says "when the gate is red"; the condition is any earlier failed step
- **Location:** `.github/workflows/ci.yml:36, 44`
- **Description:** `if: failure()` also fires when the dependency or systemd step fails. The keep dir then does not exist and the upload only warns.
- **Suggested fix:** Reword the comment. `if-no-files-found: error` (above) makes that case visible.

- **Title:** Pre-existing, not from this commit: the gate's shellcheck verdict depends on the caller's cwd
- **Location:** `tests/run:38-54`
- **Description:** On the unmodified HEAD copy with the var unset, running `<copy>/tests/run <fixture>` from a directory other than the repo root gave `GATE: FAIL passed=1 failed=1 shellcheck=fail` (SC2034 at `tests/20-dead-child.sh:97`). The same command from the repo root gave `PASS shellcheck (33 files)`. Cause inferred, not proven: `# shellcheck source=` paths resolve against the cwd. `scripts/gate.sh` and CI both run from the root.
- **Suggested fix:** `cd "$REPO"` before the shellcheck call, in a separate change.

### Validated

- **Confirmed correct:**
  - The reviewed files are the committed ones: `git diff HEAD -- <4 files>` gives 0 lines; HEAD is 10d228d13678.
  - The new block passes on HEAD: lines 10 and 25-37 of `tests/00-harness.sh` run standalone (no `lib.sh`, no `systemctl`) against the copy print `BLOCK-PASS`, rc=0.
  - The test fails without the implementation: with `tests/run` reverted to origin/main it stops at "keep fixture verdict: FAIL 01-ok / FAIL 02-bad". This matches the author's recorded RED.
  - 12 mutants killed, each by the named assertion:
    - no `unset BLAST_OFF_TEST_KEEP`: "keep fixture verdict"
    - no stale `rm -rf` before `mv`: "second run nested into the kept dir"
    - `cp -r` instead of `mv`: "kept work dirs also left in TMPDIR"
    - keep only failed scenarios: "passed scenario's output not kept"
    - unset branch without `rm`: "work dirs left with BLAST_OFF_TEST_KEEP unset"
    - keep only `out`: "scenario's cwd not kept"
    - keep only `cwd`: "failed scenario's output not kept"
    - no `mkdir` at all: "keep fixture verdict"
    - whole keep dir wiped per scenario: "passed scenario's output not kept"
    - kept `out` truncated: "failed scenario's output not kept"
    - kept `cwd` made unreadable: "scenario's cwd not kept"
    - (reverted file, above)
  - 5 survivors: `mkdir` without `-p`; stale kept dir wins; default keep dir when unset; `mkdir` moved into the loop; no absolutisation. The first four are findings above; no test distinguishes the fifth.
  - Criterion 1, unset: fixture run prints `GATE: PASS passed=2 failed=0 shellcheck=skipped`, rc=0. An empty-string value behaves the same.
  - Criterion 1, set: one subdir per scenario holding `out` and `cwd/`. Keep paths with spaces and a trailing slash work, and so does a symlinked keep dir. Kept dir mode is 700, `out` 644.
  - The var is hidden from nested runs (the CI configuration): the new block run as scenario `00-drv` under an outer `BLAST_OFF_TEST_KEEP` gives `PASS 00-drv`. The outer keep dir holds only `00-drv`; the inner fixtures sit in `outer/00-drv/cwd/kept` (`01-ok 02-bad`).
  - Criterion 2, statically: `ci.yml:35-37` sets the var on the `tests/run` step; `ci.yml:43-48` is an `actions/upload-artifact@v4` step with `if: failure()` and the same path. The `runner` context is available in `jobs.<job_id>.steps.env` and `steps.with`, and not in `jobs.<job_id>.env` ([contexts table](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/contexts)), so step-level placement is the valid one.
  - Criterion 3: `tests/run:7-8` documents the var. `docs/spec.md:215` names the behaviour in the `00-harness` row. No other file documents `tests/run` env vars (repo-wide grep for `BLAST_OFF_TEST_TIMEOUT` hits only `tests/run`).
  - Criterion 4: the test covers both ways, with the limits listed under MEDIUM and LOW.
  - `run.log` is inside the kept tree: `bin/blast-off:60` sets `LOG="$JOB/run.log"` and `tests/lib.sh:23` puts `JOB` under the scenario cwd.
  - Tokens in kept output are dummies: every scenario exports `GH_TOKEN=dummy-not-a-token`.
  - Hidden files: a grep of `tests/*.sh` shows the only dot path created under a scenario cwd is `.git`, which the upload's default `include-hidden-files: false` leaves out.
  - Dependency facts: `gh api` shows `action.yml` at `v4` has `using: 'node20'` and at `v7` `using: 'node24'`; tag `v4` resolves to `ea165f8d...`.

- **Examined, inconclusive:**
  - `.github/workflows/ci.yml:43-48`: whether the upload step works on a hosted runner. Blocker: the branch is unpushed and the step has never executed; `actionlint` is not installed here.
  - `ci.yml:45`: whether `upload-artifact@v4` runs correctly when forced onto Node 24. Blocker: needs a red CI run.
  - `ci.yml:14, 44`: whether `failure()` fires on job timeout or cancel. Blocker: the docs page does not say.
  - `tests/run:34` in CI: whether `/tmp` and `runner.temp` share a filesystem (a cross-filesystem `mv` is a copy plus delete). Blocker: needs the runner. Locally both are device 2096.
  - Which filename characters `upload-artifact` rejects. Blocker: the README does not state them. The author reports none of `":<>|*?` in the kept tree; I did not see that tree.
  - Re-run of a failed job reusing the artifact name `blast-off-tests`. The README says the action fails when an artifact of that name exists and `overwrite` is false. Blocker: whether a re-run attempt counts as the same run is not stated.

- **Not examined:**
  - A coverage percentage. The role's 80% target has no bash tool here and I did not invent a number.
  - The other 17 scenarios' behaviour beyond grep. I ran neither the full suite nor any real scenario, per the experiment rules.
  - The full `00-harness.sh` end to end. I ran only its new block standalone, to avoid `lib.sh`'s `systemctl --user stop` trap.
  - The gate log at `baton-runner/br-1115-issues/gate-phase-1-iter-1/tests-run.log`. It shows `GATE: PASS passed=18 failed=0 shellcheck=ok` but carries no commit id and no record of whether the var was set.
  - The author's full-suite run with the var set (18 subdirs, 8.4M, no sockets or FIFOs).
  - The rest of `docs/spec.md` for accuracy. I read it in full but checked only line 215 against behaviour.

### Confidence

High for criteria 1, 3 and 4 (measured by mutation and probes on a HEAD copy); medium for criterion 2, which only a deliberately red CI run on the pushed branch would raise.
